newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bundesbank sets 5-day quick repo tender at 3 pct.
newsitem.headline: Bundesbank sets 5-day quick repo tender at 3 pct.

text.p: The Bundesbank said on Friday it was offering the money market additional liquidity by setting a so-called quick securities repurchase tender with a five day maturity at at fixed three percent rate.

Traders had expected the move after money market rates had traded up to 3.20 percent on Thursday and they scrambled to meet the Bundesbank's higher than expected monthly minimum reserve target for January.
At its regular weekly tender allocation on Wednesday the Bundesbank offered banks 74.2 billion marks in liquidity.
Money market dealers had said that amount had been meagre in light of the 40-billion marks($24.5 billion) reserve target, which topped dealers' expectations by one to two billion marks.
The Bundesbank rarely resorts to injecting additional money market liqudity through a quick-tender.
Funds are generally credited to banks a few hours after the Bundesbank calls for tenders, and they usually remain in the market between three and five days.
